headline: Waymo and Toyota build robotaxis on Toyota's factory line for Tokyo launch
summary: Waymo's self-driving technology will be integrated directly into Toyota bZ4X electric SUVs on the assembly line, with services planned for Tokyo in 2027.
details: Waymo has announced that its robotaxi service, launching in Tokyo in 2027, will utilize Toyota bZ4X electric vehicles. This initiative is a significant step in the ongoing strategic partnership between Waymo and Toyota, first established in April 2025.

The bZ4X robotaxis will be manufactured at Toyota's Takaoka plant in Japan. Crucially, Waymo's self-driving sensors and computers will be installed directly on the assembly line, a departure from the previous method of retrofitting completed vehicles.

This new approach to vehicle integration is expected to streamline production, reduce redundant labor, and potentially lower costs for Waymo. It also demonstrates the adaptability of Waymo's autonomous driving technology across a diverse range of vehicle platforms.

Waymo plans to commence initial testing and validation of these vehicles in Japan next year. Following this phase, the robotaxis are slated for rollout in the United Kingdom and other international markets.

Beyond robotaxi services, Waymo is also exploring the integration of its technology into Toyota vehicles for personally owned autonomous cars. The company is collaborating with Woven by Toyota to enhance road safety using operational and safety telemetry data.
